content: The dataset contains 205,785 bookings and 14,939 unique customers recorded between February 1, 2025, and February 28, 2026.
Kitchen Cleaning (Standard tier) generated the highest gross value of ₹4,983,894, while Laundry (Standard tier) had the highest volume with 13,433 bookings.
The average booking value (GMV) is consistently approximately ₹440 across all five hubs, with a average contribution margin of 23%.
On-time arrival performance shows a massive urban-rural divide: Metropolitan areas achieve 52.23% on-time rates compared to just 2.98% in Semi-Urban areas.
SMS campaigns achieve the highest open rate at 94.91% (assumed), but WhatsApp is the primary scale driver with 595,622 sends and a 0.44% conversion rate.
The growth funnel shows high initial intent with 18,000 signups, but significant retention decay as only 1,118 customers reach their third booking within 30 days.
Operational flags indicate that 40% of all bookings (82,202) involve a promotional campaign, highlighting a heavy reliance on discounting for volume.
In-app messaging is the most efficient conversion channel with a rate of 0.61%, despite having the lowest send volume (18,380).
Average arrival time is 10.48 minutes in Metropolitan areas, closely aligning with the target SLA of 10 minutes.
Commission rates are tiered by service complexity: Quick services (30m) are charged at 25-27% while Premium services (120m) reach 30-32%.
Contribution margin is calculated by deducting payment fees, promo costs, referral rewards, and allocated support costs from the commission earned.
A 'frequency_cap_hit' flag in the comms_full view indicates the message was suppressed; these rows must be excluded when calculating delivery costs or CTR.
Retention for on-demand home services is typically measured by the 'second_booking_14d' milestone, which signals the transition from trial to habitual use.
The platform uses last-touch attribution for CRM, where 'converted' is true only if a booking is made within 24 hours of a click event.
Partner earnings are net of commission and penalties but inclusive of incentives; net payout is settled weekly every Wednesday (T+3).
High cancellation or rescheduling rates (currently ~7,000 rows) often correlate with high traffic density or extreme weather events like storms.
The platform take rate of ~28% is in line with global home-service industry standards of 20-30% (e.g., Urban Company, TaskRabbit).
An NPS of 29 is considered healthy for the gig economy, where industry benchmarks for home services generally range between 20 and 50.
A 52% on-time arrival rate in metropolitan zones is standard for on-demand services, where 10-minute SLAs are often impacted by 'last-mile' navigation.
Industry-standard CAC-to-LTV ratios for sustainable growth are typically 1:3; use the monthly_company_kpis table to monitor this ratio over time.
Referral K-factors (referral signups per active user) in successful service apps typically aim for 0.15 to 0.25 to drive organic growth.
Payment processing fees of 1.8% for cards and 0% for UPI are standard benchmarks for the Indian fintech ecosystem.
